title: I Used the Delivery App Screenshot as the Whole Argument

parts.text: I was holding a bag of still-hot biryani when the customer accused me of eating his naan. I am twenty-two, driver, I see everything. His porch light buzzed like a trapped fly. The app chat already had his essay: driver looks suspicious, food tampered, one star incoming. I had not opened the bag. The restaurant seals with a sticker that rips. His sticker was intact in my photo at pickup, timestamped. "You smell like garlic," he said from behind the storm door. I said, "You ordered garlic naan." He opened the door two inches. "Then where's the extra raita?" The ticket did not list extra raita. I showed him. He said, "I always get extra." His dog barked like it agreed. I set the bag on the chair with peeling paint, the one he used as a table. He snatched it, counted, and still looked hungry for a fight. "I'm calling support." I said, "Please do." Support pinged me while I sat in the Civic with rice-scented heat. The customer had told them I demanded cash. I had asked him to meet at the door because GPS dropped me two houses over, a known glitch on Maple. Then he posted my photo in the neighborhood group, the one from the app thumbnail, with a caption: thief. My sister texted it to me before I even put the car in gear.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: My thumbnail is in the neighborhood group as a thief while support is already in the chat.

social.video_title: He said I ate the naan on his porch — Part 1/2
social.description: A buzzing porch light, an intact seal, and a GPS pin two houses off. The neighborhood group got my thumbnail anyway. Would you have waited for support in the car?

parts.text: I sent support the pickup photo, the ticket, and the Maple GPS known-issue screenshot from the driver's forum. I sent the neighborhood admin a polite note: this is my job face, please take it down, here is the order number. The admin, a woman named Ruth, took it down and posted that accusations need more than a thumbnail. The customer one-starred me anyway. Support removed the star after three days. He ordered again two weeks later because the biryani is that good. The app showed his address. I declined. Another driver took it. I still smell garlic in the Civic. I bought a little hanging tree that does not help. My sister asked if I wanted her to comment. I said no. Ruth still waves when I deliver her groceries. The man with the storm door wrote in chat, "Drivers are so sensitive." I did not reply. I logged the GPS drop in the app the way they tell you to, every time, until Maple got a pin correction. That did more than a paragraph in a group. I eat my own naan at home, standing at the counter, which is a mundane joy I will not let a porch thief of stories take from me. He said, "Don't make this a scene." I said, "It already is."

social.video_title: Support pulled the star and Ruth pulled the post — Part 2/2
social.description: Pickup timestamps beat a thumbnail trial. I declined his next biryani. Would you have let your sister comment?
